title: Generator–Validator–Repair (GVR) loop effectiveness using deterministic reachability validation for intent→configuration
research_question: Does an LLM-driven generate–validate–repair (GVR) loop using a deterministic reachability validator increase the rate of correct, safely executable configurations (no unintended reachability changes) versus plain LLM generation on intent→configuration NetOps tasks?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The paired proportion of intents yielding correct, safely executable configurations (execution-validated) is higher after the GVR loop than for baseline plain-LLM generation (primary confirmatory hypothesis, paired analysis).

H2: Among residual failures after the GVR loop, a plurality are attributable to ambiguous or underspecified natural-language intents (specification ambiguity) rather than validator or execution defects.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do iteration counts (repairs needed) distribute across intent-complexity strata?
EQ2: What categories of validator–execution discrepancies occur (validator false negatives vs emulation-only failures)?
benchmark_scope: Public NetOps intent→config examples filtered by automated contamination checks (public datasets only)
Synthetic intent templates (deterministic, seed-controlled) to supplement filtered public tasks
Emulated device-level execution using containerized Mininet + containerized router images (Docker)
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API endpoint (deterministically prompted, single-sample generation per call); model identifier to be recorded at execution time (hosted_model_api_available).
transformation_scope: Automated repair prompt templates up to K=3 iterations
Deterministic reachability validator (containerized Batfish/pybatfish-like engine) executed in Docker
secondary_estimands: baseline_success_rate (proportion of intents with execution-validated correct configs for baseline)
validator–execution discrepancy rate (proportion of intents where validator passed but execution shows unintended reachability change)
sampling_plan: Two pre-specified scenarios (see budget_scenarios). Task selection procedure (automated): 1) harvest candidate intent→config pairs from publicly available NetOps corpora and public config repositories; 2) run automated provenance/contamination checks (string-exact, shingle Jaccard, token-overlap threshold) and exclude candidates flagged above contamination thresholds (rules below); 3) supplement with deterministically seeded synthetic intent templates to reach target N; 4) stratify tasks by intent complexity (simple/medium/complex) using an automated token/AST-based heuristic; 5) draw final N per scenario preserving strata proportions and fixed random seed (preregistered). Inclusion: tasks passing contamination filter and syntactic validity. Exclusion: automated contamination-flagged items (excluded), technical failures during dataset retrieval (logged, not counted). All selection is automated (no human review).
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by the registered 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor using estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. For each intent (paired unit): outcome 1 if execution-validated config satisfies intent and has no unintended reachability changes; 0 otherwise. Primary test: two-sided paired-proportion test (McNemar-style approximation implemented by the analysis executor) with alpha=0.05; report paired difference, 95% CI, and p-value. Primary failed_call_treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs with technical/infrastructure failures that prevent both baseline and guarded execution comparison); sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat failed pairs conservatively as failures). Secondary analyses (exploratory): descriptive failure-mode breakdown, iteration-count histograms, validator–execution discrepancy contingency tables; exploratory subgroup tests will have multiplicity-adjustment (Benjamini–Hochberg) and be reported as exploratory.
multiplicity_plan: Single pre-registered primary paired test (family-wise control not required). All subgroup and secondary comparisons are exploratory and will be corrected with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR for presented p-values; no exploratory result will be elevated to confirmatory claims.
missingness_plan: Pairs with technical infrastructure failures (model API outages, container execution errors preventing both baseline and guarded execution traces) will be logged and excluded under the primary analysis ('complete_pair_primary'). We will report counts and run the prespecified sensitivity analysis treating excluded pairs as failures. All exclusions and technical-retry attempts will be recorded with timestamps and hashes; retry policy: up to 2 automated retries for transient API or container startup failures separated by exponential backoff, after which the pair is logged as a technical failure.

risk_factors: Exact/config-template duplication present in LLM training data
High token-overlap with public config fragments
Common ACL or route snippets that are widely reposted
detection_procedures: Exact-string matches against harvested public corpora and public GitHub configs (automated)
Shingle-based Jaccard similarity (k=8 tokens) between candidate intent+config and public corpora; compute token-level overlap fraction
Token-overlap threshold via byte-pair tokenizer token overlap fraction against public corpora
item_flagging_rules: Flag and exclude if exact-string match of candidate config (>=95% exact) with any public corpus item
Flag and exclude if shingle Jaccard similarity >= 0.6 with any public corpus item
Flag for caution (not auto-exclude) if token-overlap fraction between 0.3 and 0.6; flagged items are moved to deterministic synthetic augmentation instead of inclusion
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes items automatically flagged for contamination. We will report separate exploratory analyses including flagged items and report effect-size differences. All contamination decisions are deterministic and logged; no human adjudication is used.
residual_uncertainty: Automated heuristics cannot guarantee zero training-data leakage; residual contamination may remain below flagging thresholds.
Contamination heuristics are conservative; some common templated configs may be excluded, biasing toward harder tasks.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimum-budget confirmatory run (preregistered minimal N meeting reviewer repair request: N=200). Conservative exclusions and synthetic supplementation; K=3 repair iterations allowed; worst-case model-call planning.
models: hosted-llm-api (single selected endpoint; identifier recorded at execution)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case model calls = N * (1 baseline + up to 3 repairs) = 200 * 4 = 800 model calls (within manifest limit 10,000). Docker-based validator and Mininet emulation run on CPU nodes; expected wall time per pair measured in preregistration estimates. Planned retries and automated logging fit within the 7-day wall-clock execution budget with parallel Docker task scheduling.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended powered confirmatory run (N=300) to target 80% power to detect a 10 percentage-point absolute increase under conservative discordant-pair assumptions.
models: hosted-llm-api (single selected endpoint; identifier recorded at execution)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case model calls = 300 * 4 = 1200 (within manifest cap 10,000). Power calculations (see power_plan) justify N=300; Docker-based validator (pybatfish-like) and containerized Mininet/router images execute on available CPU infrastructure in parallel batches. All actions automated; no human labor required.

power_plan.clustering_unit: intent (paired baseline vs guarded per intent)
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal-approximation McNemar-style paired-proportion sample-size approximation using assumed discordant-pair fraction
assumptions: Estimated discordant-pair fraction (p01 + p10) = 0.35 based on prior literature and conservative pilot heuristics
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: Under stated assumptions (discordant fraction 0.35), required N ≈ 274; recommended N=300 provides margin for exclusions and technical failures.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power under discordant fractions 0.25 and 0.45 and report achieved detectable effect-size at fixed N=300.
Sensitivity analysis treating technical failures as failures (worst-case) and recalculating paired difference and CIs.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Unit tests for validator: a synthetic suite of N_unit=100 deterministic topology/config mutations with known intended reachability changes; compare validator verdicts to emulation execution traces to estimate validator false-negative and false-positive rates
Post-processing check: parser round-trip (config→AST→config) equality test
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject transformed config if syntax sanitizer yields unfixable vendor syntax errors
Reject repair output if validator raises parse/unsupported-feature exception; record as repair failure and continue per retry policy
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Audit 10% random sample of accepted mapped intents/configs by re-running validator and emulation under alternative seeds and report discrepancies (automated re-execution, deterministic logging).
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Deterministic unit tests (synthetic cases) and systematic validator-vs-emulation comparison to estimate validator misclassification rate; results drive conservative interpretation of validator-assisted success.
residual_risks: Validator may have non-zero false-negative rate (missed unintended reachability changes) even after unit tests; such residual risk will be quantified and reported.
Emulation (Mininet + container images) may not capture all vendor-specific behaviors; this remains a noncritical external-validity limitation.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Residual possibility of training-data contamination below automated detection thresholds (may inflate baseline success rates); handled by exclusion heuristics and sensitivity analyses.

Validator completeness limits: deterministic reachability validator may not model some vendor-specific data-plane behaviors; unit tests and validator–execution discrepancy logging quantify this risk but cannot fully eliminate emulation-vs-real-device gaps.
Emulation realism: containerized router images + Mininet approximate many behaviors but may omit proprietary device quirks; external generalization to production devices is out of scope.
